correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the comparison. For nonzero x, dilate x by V(x)^(-1/(d+mu)) to the compact nonempty level set K (properness and homogeneity); on K the positive continuous F has minimum m>0. Rescaling gives F(x)>=m V(x)^(d/(d+mu)), with equality on the rays through the minimizers. The optimal HJB feedback gives dV/dt=-F-|u|^q/q. Integrate the inequality for V^(mu/(d+mu)) while V is positive; once V is zero, nonnegativity and monotonicity keep it zero. This includes x=0. For the example the weights (7/5,6/5) give degree 2 and satisfy the strict parameter constraint; the powers exceed 1. Constancy on K would imply V=C F^(11/10), whose last derivative vanishes at (s,0), s!=0. The drift there is also zero, contradicting HJB. Therefore max_K F is an upper, not lower, coefficient for F, in a genuinely admissible example. This does not refute a bound that could exploit the control-cost term.
